questions.title: Question 1: Information Attraction
questions.text: What type of information naturally captures your attention?

options.A: Data, statistics, research findings, and factual analysis
options.B: How things work, technical processes, and systematic explanations
options.C: People's stories, experiences, and interpersonal dynamics
options.D: New trends, creative concepts, and innovative possibilities

questions.title: Question 2: Reading Preferences
questions.text: When choosing something to read, you're naturally drawn to:

options.A: Research reports, analytical articles, and evidence-based content
options.B: Technical manuals, how-to guides, and detailed explanations
options.C: Biographies, human interest stories, and relationship-focused content
options.D: Creative works, futuristic concepts, and imaginative possibilities

questions.title: Question 3: Conversation Engagement
questions.text: You become most engaged in conversations about:

options.A: Facts, theories, and logical analysis of complex topics
options.B: Practical solutions, methods, and how to accomplish things
options.C: Personal experiences, relationships, and human emotions
options.D: Ideas, possibilities, and creative or innovative concepts

questions.title: Question 4: Learning Curiosity
questions.text: You're most curious to learn about:

options.A: Why things happen and what evidence supports different conclusions
options.B: How systems function and what makes processes work effectively
options.C: What motivates people and how relationships develop and change
options.D: What's possible in the future and how new ideas might be applied

questions.title: Question 5: Problem Interest
questions.text: You're naturally drawn to problems involving:

options.A: Research, investigation, and finding truth through analysis
options.B: Troubleshooting, optimization, and making things work better
options.C: Understanding people, resolving conflicts, and improving relationships
options.D: Innovation, creativity, and discovering new approaches

questions.title: Question 6: Documentary Preferences
questions.text: You'd be most interested in watching documentaries about:

options.A: Scientific discoveries, historical analysis, or investigative journalism
options.B: Engineering marvels, manufacturing processes, or skill development
options.C: Human stories, cultural studies, or social dynamics
options.D: Artistic movements, future technologies, or creative innovations

questions.title: Question 7: Curiosity Triggers
questions.text: Your curiosity is most triggered by:

options.A: Questions that can be answered through research and logical analysis
options.B: Challenges that require figuring out practical solutions and methods
options.C: Situations involving human behavior, emotions, and relationships
options.D: Opportunities to explore new ideas and creative possibilities

questions.title: Question 8: Information Processing
questions.text: When encountering new information, you're most interested in:

options.A: Evaluating its accuracy, sources, and logical consistency
options.B: Understanding its practical applications and implementation
options.C: Considering its impact on people and relationships
options.D: Exploring its creative potential and future possibilities

questions.title: Question 9: Hobby Attractions
questions.text: Your hobbies and interests tend to involve:

options.A: Research, analysis, collecting data, or studying complex subjects
options.B: Building, fixing, crafting, or developing practical skills
options.C: Social activities, helping others, or understanding human nature
options.D: Creative expression, exploring new experiences, or innovative projects

questions.title: Question 10: Question Types
questions.text: You're most likely to ask questions like:

options.A: "What does the research show?" or "What's the evidence for this?"
options.B: "How does this work?" or "What's the best way to do this?"
options.C: "How do people feel about this?" or "What's the impact on relationships?"
options.D: "What if we tried something different?" or "What possibilities does this open up?"

questions.title: Question 11: News Interest
questions.text: In news and current events, you're most drawn to:

options.A: In-depth analysis, investigative reporting, and fact-checking
options.B: Practical implications, policy details, and implementation strategies
options.C: Human interest stories, social impact, and community effects
options.D: Emerging trends, innovative solutions, and future implications

questions.title: Question 12: Museum Preferences
questions.text: At a museum, you'd spend most time in sections about:

options.A: Historical research, scientific discoveries, or analytical exhibits
options.B: Technology, engineering, or demonstrations of how things work
options.C: Cultural artifacts, human stories, or social history
options.D: Art, design, or exhibits about innovation and creativity

questions.title: Question 13: Online Browsing
questions.text: When browsing online, you're most likely to click on:

options.A: Research articles, analytical pieces, or fact-based content
options.B: How-to guides, tutorials, or practical advice articles
options.C: Personal stories, social content, or relationship advice
options.D: Creative content, trend articles, or innovative ideas

questions.title: Question 14: Expertise Development
questions.text: You're most motivated to develop expertise in areas that involve:

options.A: Research methods, analytical thinking, or evidence evaluation
options.B: Technical skills, practical applications, or systematic processes
options.C: Understanding people, communication, or relationship building
options.D: Creative thinking, innovation, or exploring new possibilities

questions.title: Question 15: Discussion Preferences
questions.text: In group discussions, you're most engaged when talking about:

options.A: Facts, research findings, and logical analysis of issues
options.B: Practical solutions, implementation strategies, and methods
options.C: Personal experiences, human impact, and relationship dynamics
options.D: New ideas, creative approaches, and future possibilities

questions.title: Question 16: Information Seeking
questions.text: When you need to understand something new, you first look for:

options.A: Research studies, expert analysis, and evidence-based explanations
options.B: Step-by-step guides, practical examples, and how-to information
options.C: Personal testimonials, case studies, and human experiences
options.D: Creative examples, innovative approaches, and possibility thinking

questions.title: Question 17: Workplace Interest
questions.text: At work, you're most interested in projects involving:

options.A: Data analysis, research, or investigating complex questions
options.B: Process improvement, system optimization, or practical problem-solving
options.C: Team development, stakeholder engagement, or people-focused initiatives
options.D: Innovation, creative problem-solving, or exploring new approaches

questions.title: Question 18: Learning Style
questions.text: You learn best when information is presented through:

options.A: Research findings, logical arguments, and analytical frameworks
options.B: Practical examples, demonstrations, and step-by-step processes
options.C: Stories, case studies, and human examples
options.D: Creative metaphors, visual concepts, and imaginative scenarios

questions.title: Question 19: Attention Span
questions.text: You can maintain attention longest when content involves:

options.A: Deep analysis, research exploration, or logical investigation
options.B: Practical application, skill development, or systematic learning
options.C: Human stories, interpersonal dynamics, or social situations
options.D: Creative possibilities, innovative concepts, or imaginative scenarios

questions.title: Question 20: Intellectual Stimulation
questions.text: You feel most intellectually stimulated by:

options.A: Analyzing complex data and drawing evidence-based conclusions
options.B: Understanding how systems work and optimizing their performance
options.C: Exploring human behavior and improving interpersonal relationships
options.D: Imagining new possibilities and creating innovative solutions

A.name: Analytical & Research-Focused
A.summary: You are drawn to data, facts, research, and logical analysis. You want to understand evidence and how conclusions are reached.
scoring_bullets: Data & research curiosity. Evidence, proof, logical investigation; thrives with research databases, systematic analysis, and evidence-based content.

B.name: Practical & Systems-Focused
B.summary: You are interested in how things work, technical details, and practical applications. You like solving real problems.
scoring_bullets: Systems & process curiosity. How things work, practical application, skill development; thrives with hands-on learning and technical problem-solving.

C.name: People & Experience-Focused
C.summary: You are curious about people, stories, and human experience. You engage with ideas through conversation and narrative.
scoring_bullets: Human & social curiosity. Human behavior, relationship dynamics, social impact; thrives with stories, collaboration, and understanding people.

D.name: Creative & Big-Picture Focused
D.summary: You are drawn to creative expression, trends, and broader implications. You like connecting ideas and seeing the bigger picture.
scoring_bullets: Innovation & possibility curiosity. New ideas, creative solutions, future orientation; thrives with creative expression and exploring possibilities.

scoring_intro: Step 1: Count your responses for each letter: A (Analytical Interest), B (Technical Interest), C (People Interest), D (Creative Interest). Step 2: Determine your interest driver pattern from the ranges below..
mixed_results: Dual Interest Driver: 8–12 in two categories (e.g. A+B Research Engineer, C+D Social Innovator). Balanced: 6–10 across three or more = combination pattern. Multi-Domain Curiosity: 5–8 in each = balanced across all four. See combination profiles below.
